issues: The footage was the generic FakeDashboard, so the three flashes 'crowned' a meaningless $48.2k with no sense of an awards moment
On a light grey stage the white flash barely popped; there was too little contrast between flash and picture
Nothing set up the flashes, so they felt random, and the frozen stills didn't contrast enough with the live footage before them
The 4x number close-up was cropped against the card edge, with an off-balance composition and messy negative space
changes: Graphite look: the scene is now an awards backdrop (a brick-tiled OSTRA / GOLDEN PIXEL step-and-repeat) behind an 'App of the Year · No.1 in 38 countries · Ostra Maps' card, with champagne gold reserved for the award details
You are the camera: a screen-space viewfinder HUD (corner frame, 1/250 F2.8 ISO 1600, shot counter 023 to 026, a flash charge ring), and the white flash hits hard on the dark stage
An anticipation beat: 8f before each flash the AF brackets shrink from 1.3x onto the next crop and lock champagne 3f before firing; after the flash the counter ticks and the charge ring resets

Live versus frozen: for 30f before the first flash, other photographers' star flashes pop across the backdrop under a slow push; every still afterwards is slightly desaturated and contrasty, so it reads as a photo
The three crops are rebuilt as 1.0 wide, 1.6 card and 2.8 'No.1', never cutting a line of text; the 70f hold has only a 1 to 1.015 push, with a 'SAVED' tick fading in from 84f
